title: Deep Pipeline Embeddings for AutoML

problem.claim: AutoML requires optimizing machine-learning pipelines across choices such as preprocessing, augmentations, models, and optimizers.

gap.claim: Existing pipeline-optimization methods do not examine deep interactions among pipeline stages and components.

contributions.claim: A neural architecture captures deep interactions between machine-learning pipeline components.
Pipelines are embedded into a latent representation using a per-component encoder mechanism.
Pipeline embeddings are used in deep-kernel Gaussian-process surrogates within Bayesian optimization, with embedding parameters meta-learned from evaluations on related datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper explicitly presents its neural architecture and per-component encoder mechanism as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments were conducted on three large-scale meta-datasets.
The authors report that pipeline embeddings achieve state-of-the-art results in pipeline optimization.

narrative_sequence.summary: AutoML aims to automate machine-learning system deployment with minimal human expertise.
The technical challenge is optimizing the components of machine-learning pipelines.
Existing methods do not adequately explore deep interactions among pipeline stages and components.
The paper introduces pipeline embeddings, deep-kernel Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization, and meta-learning from related-dataset evaluations.
The authors report state-of-the-art pipeline-optimization results across three large-scale meta-datasets.

source_observation.claim: Pipeline embeddings are used to represent pipeline components and their interactions for Bayesian optimization.

interpretation.claim: A structured latent representation may help optimization methods model interactions that component-wise search misses.

application.claim: For complex configurable workflows, consider learning representations of component combinations before surrogate-based search.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when pipeline embeddings outperform alternatives outside the reported evaluation setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative margins of improvement.
The abstract does not describe the neural architecture or per-component encoder in implementation detail.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
